newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC BECOMES FOURTH SEED TO FALL AT FIRST HURDLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC BECOMES FOURTH SEED TO FALL AT FIRST HURDLE.

text.p: Fifth seed Goran Ivanisevic, the 1993 champion, became on Wednesday the fourth seeded player to fall at the first hurdle in the Paris Open when he lost 6-3 6-2 to Paul Haarhuis.
The Dutch doubles specialist took just 54 minutes to beat the Croatian for the fifth time in succession and seventh overall in 10 meetings in their second round match.
Three other seeded players --Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek, Andre Agassi and Jim Courier -- each lost their second round matches on Tuesday.
Haarhuis, ranked 24 places below world number five Ivanisevic, outplayed the Coatian in all departments including sending down five aces to his opponent's uncharacteristically meagre total of three.
Ivanisevic, one of only five players to have secured a place in the eight-man ATP Tour World Championship in Hanover next month, also served seven double faults.
In the third round, Haarhuis comes up against 11th-seeded American Todd Martin, one of several players vying for the remaining three places in Hanover.
